Listed at {{convert|6|ft|7|in|m|2}} and {{convert|181|lbs|kg|0}}, he plays the [[point guard]] position. Ball began high school at [[Chino Hills High School]] in [[Chino Hills, California]], where he won a state championship and achieved national success as a freshman with his older brothers [[Lonzo Ball|Lonzo]], now an NBA guard, and [[LiAngelo Ball|LiAngelo]]. Before his junior season, a coaching dispute prompted him to leave Chino Hills and sign with Lithuanian professional team [[BC Prienai|Prienai]]. In 2018, he played in the [[Junior Basketball Association]] (JBA), a league created by his father, before returning to high school as a senior with [[SPIRE Institute and Academy|SPIRE Academy]] in [[Geneva, Ohio]]. A former [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] commit, he was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] but chose to forgo college basketball amid eligibility concerns and play for the [[The Hawks (NBL)|Illawarra Hawks]] in 2019, winning [[NBL Rookie of the Year Award|NBL Rookie of the Year]]. Ball and his brothers have attracted national attention since playing together in high school. His father, [[LaVar Ball|LaVar]], also grew into a [[celebrity|media personality]] in 2017. Ball has a signature shoe by his father's company, [[Big Baller Brand]], and a role on his family's [[Facebook Watch]] reality show ''[[Ball in the Family]]''. ==Early life== Ball was trained in [[basketball]] by his father, [[LaVar Ball|LaVar]], as soon as he could walk.{{cite web |last1=Palmer |first1=Chris |title=The extraordinary life of LaMelo Ball |url=https://theundefeated.com/features/the-extraordinary-life-of-lamelo-ball/ |publisher=[[The Undefeated (website)|The Undefeated]] |accessdate=April 26, 2020 |date=March 8, 2018}} At age four, he started playing the sport with his older brothers, [[Lonzo Ball|Lonzo]] and [[LiAngelo Ball|LiAngelo]], facing much older opponents. He also played [[flag football]] with his brothers at age five but continued to focus on basketball.{{cite web|last1=Stephens|first1=Mitch|title=The Architect: Father of the Ball brothers speaks about growth of Chino Hills|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/jHzX-KpBGky5RKqc8SXiYA/the-architect--father-of-the-ball-brothers-speaks-about-growth-of-chino-hills.htm|website=MaxPreps.com|accessdate=February 8, 2017|date=March 26, 2016}} In 2013, while in seventh grade, Ball began playing with his brothers on Big Ballers VXT, a 17-and-under [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) team launched and coached by his parents.{{cite web|last1=Parrish|first1=Gary|title=The Ball family -- coming to a basketball court (and TV) near you|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/the-ball-family-coming-to-a-basketball-court-and-tv-near-you/|website=[[CBS Sports]]|accessdate=February 8, 2017|date=June 30, 2015}} The team, which was not sponsored by a major shoe company, did not compete in top AAU circuits and instead took part in local competitions.{{cite web |last1=Calle |first1=Franklyn |title=Lonzo, LiAngelo and LaMelo Ball are About to Take Over the Basketball World |url=https://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/ball-bros/ |website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |accessdate=April 26, 2020 |date=August 4, 2016}} ==High school career== ===Freshman=== In his freshman season, Ball started playing basketball for [[Chino Hills High School]] in [[Chino Hills, California]]. He was teammates with his two older brothers, Lonzo and LiAngelo, and his cousin, Andre Ball.{{cite web|last1=Sondheimer|first1=Eric|title=It's Ball in the family at Chino Hills basketball|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/la-sp-ball-brothers-sondheimer-20150427-column.html|website=[[Los Angeles Times]]|accessdate=February 8, 2017|date=April 26, 2015}} In his first game, Ball scored 27 points as a starter.{{Cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-vi-boys-basketball-freshman-lamelo-ball-makes-quite-a-debut-for-chino-hills-20150616-story.html |title=Boys' basketball: LaMelo Ball, 13, makes quite a debut for Chino Hill |last=Sondheimer |first=Eric |date=June 16, 2015 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=February 8, 2017}} On March 5, 2016, he scored 26 points in a win over [[Sierra Canyon School]] for the [[CIF Southern Section]] Open Division title.{{cite web|last1=Sondheimer|first1=Eric|title=Chino Hills defeats Sierra Canyon, 105-83, for first section title|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/la-sp-chino-hills-sierra-canyon-20160306-column.html|website=[[Los Angeles Times]]|accessdate=February 8, 2017|date=March 5, 2016}} Later in the month, Ball helped his team capture the CIF Open Division state championship, recording 14 points in the title game against [[De La Salle High School (Concord, California)|De La Salle High School]]. Chino Hills finished the season with a 35–0 record and claimed the [[mythical national championship]].{{cite web|last1=Stephens|first1=Mitch|title=Top-ranked Chino Hills finishes perfect season with a flurry|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/j_MSlbiD1UeuK8wsiJPZOA/top-ranked-chino-hills-finishes-perfect-season-with-a-flurry.htm|website=MaxPreps.com|accessdate=February 8, 2017|date=March 27, 2017}} Ball averaged 16.4 points and 3.8 assists per game and shared [[MaxPreps National Basketball Player of the Year awards#Freshman of the Year|MaxPreps National Freshman of the Year]] honors with his teammate, [[Onyeka Okongwu]].{{cite web|last1=Borzello|first1=Jeff|title=Lonzo is just the beginning of the Ball-UCLA pipeline|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/18268717/ucla-bruins-lonzo-ball-family-just-beginning-relationship|website=[[ESPN]]|accessdate=February 8, 2017|date=December 14, 2018|date=December 12, 2017}} The brothers' move to Lithuania was heavily reported by American sports media.{{cite web|last1=Chavez|first1=Chris|title=LaVar Ball and Family Arrive In Lithuania, Mobbed web|last1=Skiver|first1=Kevin|last2=Ward-Henninger|first2=Colin|title=LiAngelo and LaMelo Ball make Lithuanian basketball debut: 6 strangest takeaways|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/liangelo-and-lamelo-ball-make-lithuanian-basketball-debut-6-strangest-takeaways/|website=[[CBSSports.com]]|accessdate=January 20, 2018|date=January 9, 2018}} On February 4, he scored a season-high 19 points, with four three-pointers and six assists, in a loss to [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris]].{{cite web|title="Žalgirio" nepabūgę ballai sužaidė geriausias rungtynes ir padėjo "Vytautui" pagerinti rekordą|url=http://en.lkl.lt/straipsniai/1380/zalgirio-nepabuge-ballai-suzaide-geriausias-rungtynes-ir-padejo-vytautui-pagerinti-rekorda|website=LKL.lt|accessdate=February 4, 2018|date=February 4, Returns from Injury in BC Vytautas' Loss|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2766500-liangelo-ball-hits-6-3-pointers-lamelo-returns-from-injury-in-bc-vytautas-loss|publisher=[[Bleacher |url=https://lonzowire.usatoday.com/2018/02/26/lamelo-ball-hurt-lithuania-big-baller-brand-challenge/ |publisher=Lonzo Wire |date=February 26, 2018}} On April 25, Ball left Prienai with his family, with his father criticizing the team's head coach [[Virginijus Šeškus]], in part because Ball did not receive enough playing time.{{cite web |title=LiAngelo and LaMelo Ball leave BC Vytautas due to injuries |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23317012/battling-injuries-liangelo-lamelo-ball-leave-lithuania-bc-vytautas |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=July 1, 2018 |date=April 26, 2018}}{{cite |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/early-lead/wp/2018/04/25/lavar-ball-is-pulling-sons-liangelo-and-lamelo-out-of-lithuania-before-season-ends/?noredirect=on |website=[[The Washington Post]] |accessdate=July 1, 2018 |date=April 25, 2018}} He finished the LKL season averaging 6.5 points and 2.4 assists, shooting 26.8 percent from the field, in 12.8 minutes per game.{{cite web |title=LaMelo Ball Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/LaMelo-Ball/Summary/103892 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=July 1, 2018}} ===Los Angeles Ballers (2018)=== On May 4, 2018, Ball signed with the [[Los Angeles Ballers]] of the [[Junior Basketball Association]] (JBA), a new league created by his father as an alternative to college basketball, and was touted by the league as its "marquee player."{{cite web |last1=Martin |first1=Josh |title=LaMelo Ball signs with Los Angeles Ballers as JBA's 'MARQUEE Player' |url=https://lonzowire.usatoday.com/2018/06/12/lamelo-ball-los-angeles-ballers-jba-league-marquee-player/ |publisher=Lonzo Wire |date=June 12, 2018}}{{cite web |last1=Calle |first1=Franklyn |title=LaMelo Ball Will Join The JBA League This Summer |url=https://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/high-school/lamelo-ball-will-joining-jba-league-summer/ |website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |accessdate=July 1, 2018 |date=May 4, 2018}} In his debut on June 21, he posted a triple-double of 40 points, 16 rebounds, 10 assists and three steals, shooting 15-of-40 from the field, in a 134–124 win over the [[New York Ballers]].{{cite web |last1=Newport |first1=Kyle |title=LaMelo Ball Scores 40 in LA Baller's Junior Basketball Association Win |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2782353-lamelo-ball-scores-40-in-la-ballers-junior-basketball-association-win |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |accessdate=July 1, 2018 |date=June 22, 2018}}{{cite web |title=FIBA LiveStats |url=http://www.fibalivestats.com/u/JBA/885625/ |publisher=FIBA Live Stats |accessdate=July 1, 2018}} Over eight regular season games, Ball averaged a triple-double with 39.6 points, 14.6 rebounds and 11.5 assists per game, while being named to the All-Star Game.{{cite web |title=JBA All-Star Game |url=https://jbaleague.com/event/jba-all-star-game/ |publisher=[[Junior Basketball Association|JBA League]] |accessdate=August 1, 2018}} In the playoff semifinals versus the New York Ballers, he scored a season-high 55 points, 16 rebounds and seven assists. He led Los Angeles to a JBA championship over the [[Seattle Ballers]].{{cite web |last1=Rivas |first1=Christian |title=LiAngelo, LaMelo Ball lead Los Angeles Ballers to first-ever JBA championship |url=https://lonzowire.usatoday.com/2018/08/12/liangelo-lamelo-ball-lead-los-angeles-ballers-to-first-ever-jba-championship/ |publisher=Lonzo Wire |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |date=August 12, 2018}} After the season, Ball was named to the league's select team, called JBA USA, which would face several European teams on an international tour.{{cite web |last1=Rivas |first1=Christian |title=JBA announces international season opener, 13-man roster |url=https://lonzowire.usatoday.com/2018/09/12/lavar-ball-news-jba-international-season-liangelo-lamelo-big-baller-brand/ |publisher=Lonzo Wire |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |date=September 12, 2018}} On October 31, in an exhibition game versus [[BC Dzūkija|Dzūkija]] on the tour, he was ejected after slapping an opposing player in the face during a scuffle.{{cite web |last1=Diaz |first1=Hector |title=LaMelo Ball got ejected for slapping a Lithuanian player during a JBA game |url=https://www.sbnation.com/2018/10/1/17925778/lamelo-ball-got-ejected-for-slapping-a-lithuanian-player-during-a-jba-game |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |accessdate=May 21, 2019 |date=October 1, 2018}} On November 5, he left the JBA tour to return to high school in the United States for his senior season. ===Illawarra Hawks (2019–2020)=== [[File:LaMelo Ball Illawarra Hawks (cropped) 2.jpg|thumb|left|Ball with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] in October 2019]] On June 17, 2019, Ball signed a two-year contract, including NBA out clauses, with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the Australian-based [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL).{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=LaMelo Ball commits to play in Australian NBL |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/26994195/lamelo-ball-commits-play-australian-nbl |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=June 18, 2019 |date=June 17, 2019}} He joined the Hawks through the NBL Next Stars program, which aims to develop [[NBA draft]] prospects.{{cite web |title=Illawarra Hawks Sign Lamelo Ball |url=http://www.hawks.com.au/news/article/illawarra-hawks-sign-lamelo-ball |publisher=[[Illawarra Hawks]] |accessdate=June 17, 2019 |date=June 17, 2019}}{{cite web |title=NBL to Fast Track Next Stars of the NBA |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/nbl-to-fast-track-next-stars-of-the-nba |publisher=[[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] |accessdate=May 29, 2019 |date=March 2, 2018}} In August 2019, after playing for No Shnacks at the [[Drew League]], Ball was named Leader of the New School, an award honoring the league's top rookie.{{cite web |title=2019 Drew League Award Winners |url=http://www.drewleague.com/blog/2019/08/19/2019-drew-league-award-winners/ |publisher=[[Drew League]] |accessdate=May 6, 2020 |date=August 19, 2019}} For the NBL season, he moved to Australia with his former SPIRE Institute coach Jermaine Jackson, who became his manager and helped him acclimate. In late September, he had success at the [[2019–20 NBL pre-season#2019 NBL Blitz Tasmania|NBL Blitz]], a pre-season tournament. He recorded 19 points, 13 rebounds and seven assists in a preseason win over the [[Perth Wildcats]].{{cite web |title=NBA Scouts Heap Praise On LaMelo Ball After NBL Blitz |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/nba-scouts-heap-praise-on-lamelo-ball-after-nbl-blitz |publisher=[[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] |accessdate=October 13, 2019 |date=September 27, 2019}} On October 6, in his first regular season game, Ball tallied 12 points, 10 rebounds and five assists on 6-of-17 shooting in a loss to the [[Brisbane Bullets]].{{cite web |title=LaMelo on show, Bullets down Hawks in NBL |url=https://7news.com.au/sport/basketball/lamelo-shines-but-bullets-down-hawks-c-490111 |website=[[Seven News]] |accessdate=October 6, 2019 |date=October 6, 2019}} He assumed a more important role following a season-ending injury to star point guard [[Aaron Brooks (basketball)|Aaron Brooks]] on October 27.{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=LaMelo Ball has been on a tear over the past month in the NBL |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2019/11/29/lamelo-ball-nbl-stats-triple-double-highlights-r-j-hampton/ |website=The Rookie Wire |accessdate=December 1, 2019 |date=November 29, 2019}} Ball recorded a season-high 32 points, 11 rebounds and 13 assists on November 25, in an [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] victory over the [[Cairns Taipans]], to become the youngest NBL player to record a [[double (basketball)|triple-double]].{{cite web |title=Ball Makes History as Hawks Prevail in OT |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/ball-makes-history-as-hawks-prevail-in-ot |publisher=[[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] |accessdate=November 25, 2019 |date=November 25, 2019}} In his next game, Ball posted another triple-double with 25 points, 12 rebounds and 10 assists but was held to 10-of-28 shooting in a loss to the [[New Zealand Breakers]]. He became the fourth player in league history, and the first since the NBL switched to 40-minute games in 2009, to record consecutive triple doubles.{{cite web |last1=Pike |first1=Chris |title=DJ a Production Machine Ahead of NBL Game 250 |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/article/dj-a-production-machine-ahead-of-nbl-game-250 |publisher=[[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] |accessdate=December 1, 2019 |date=January 3, 2018}}{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=LaMelo Ball picked up another historic triple-double in the NBL |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2019/11/30/lamelo-ball-back-to-back-triple-doubles-nbl-history/ |website=The Rookie Wire |accessdate=December 1, 2019 |date=November 30, 2019}} On December 8, before he played another game, it was announced that he would miss about four weeks of action after bruising his foot in practice.{{cite web |title=LaMelo Ball Update |url=https://www.hawks.com.au/news/article/lamelo-ball-injury-update |publisher=[[Illawarra Hawks]] |accessdate=December 20, 2019 |date=December 8, 2019}} On January 16, 2020, while still sidelined, Ball decided to sit out for the remainder of the season.{{cite web |last1=West |first1=Jenna |title=LaMelo Ball Ends NBL Season in Australia Ahead of 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2020/01/16/lamelo-ball-ends-season-australia-2020-nba-draft |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=January 16, 2020 |date=January 16, 2020}} He parted ways with the Hawks on January 28 to return to the United States and prepare for the [[2020 NBA draft]]. Through 12 NBL games, Ball averaged 17 points, 7.4 rebounds and 6.8 assists per game, shooting 37.7 percent from the field.{{cite web |last1=Polacek |first1=Scott |title=LaMelo Ball Leaves NBL's Illawarra Hawks to Prepare for 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2873577-lamelo-ball-leaves-nbls-illawarra-hawks-to-prepare-for-2020-nba-draft |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |accessdate=January 28, 2020 |date=January 28, 2020}} At the end of the season, he was named [[NBL Rookie of the Year Award|NBL Rookie of the Year]] over [[Kouat Noi]] by five votes (49–44).{{cite web |last1=Uluc |first1=Olgun |title=Bryce Cotton wins MVP, LaMelo Ball takes Rookie of the Year - 2019-20 NBL Awards Recap |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/bryce-cotton-wins-mvp-lamelo-ball-takes-rookie-of-the-year-201920-nbl-awards-recap/news-story/61f3e73680d8afde485966eb00814f7b |website=[[Fox Sports (Australian TV network)|Fox Sports]] |accessdate=February 16, 2020 |date=February 16, 2020}} ===NBA=== In the days leading up to the 2020 NBA draft, Ball was considered a possible top overall pick.{{cite news |title=2020 NBA Mock Draft: LaMelo Ball is the No. 1 overall pick, goes higher than brother Lonzo Ball did |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/2020-nba-mock-draft-lamelo-ball-is-the-no-1-overall-pick-goes-higher-than-brother-lonzo-ball-did/ |work=CBSSports.com |date=November 12, 2020 |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBL=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NBL season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Illawarra Hawks season|Illawarra]] | 12 || 12 || 31.2 || .377 || .250 || .723 || 7.4 || 6.8 || 1.7 || .2 || 17.0 {{S-end}} ===LKL=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 LKL season|2017–18]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 BC Prienai season|Prienai]] | 8 || 1 || 12.8 || .268 || .250 || .737 || 1.1 || 2.4 || .8 || .1 || 6.5 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== [[File:Ball family post game.jpg|thumb|240px|Ball (right) with his father, [[LaVar Ball|LaVar]], and brother, [[LiAngelo Ball|LiAngelo]], after playing in a [[London]] exhibition game for [[BC Prienai|Prienai]] in April 2018]] Ball is the youngest son of [[LaVar Ball|LaVar]] and Tina Ball, who are both former college basketball players. LaVar, who stands 6-foot-6 (1.98 m), competed with [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]] and then [[Cal State Los Angeles Golden Eagles|Cal State Los Angeles]]. Tina, who stands 6-feet (1.83 m), also played with the latter school. Later on, LaVar played professional [[American football|football]] as a [[tight end]] for the [[London Monarchs]] of the [[NFL Europe|World League of American Football]] after being loaned from the [[New York Jets]].{{cite web|title=Transactions|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1995/03/07/sports/transactions-342895.html|website=[[The New York Times]]|accessdate=February 8, 2017|date=March 7, 1995}} In 2017, LaVar became a popular but polarizing sports [[celebrity|media personality]], primarily for making outlandish remarks about the careers of himself and his sons. Ball's oldest brother, [[Lonzo Ball|Lonzo]], is a point guard in the NBA and was the second-overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft|2017 draft]], while his other brother, [[LiAngelo Ball|LiAngelo]] has played professionally.{{cite web |last1=Olivieri |first1=Anthony |title=LaVar Ball's timeline of trolling |url=http://www.espn.com/espn/feature/story/_/id/20828896/lavar-ball-line-trolling-2017 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=May 21, 2019}} His cousin, Andre, plays college basketball for [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine]].{{cite web |last1=Giles |first1=Matt |title=Forgot About
